title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
what_happened: History > Night A - M31 > Export CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv with a populated "FWHM (px)" column - 4.70, 5.17, 5.64 - even though captured_images.fwhm is NULL for every one of those rows. The values are HFR * 2.35.
expected: For a Gaussian PSF the half-flux radius is 1.1774*sigma and FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.00 * HFR. Multiplying HFR by 2.3548 treats HFR as sigma and inflates every reported FWHM by 17.7% (HFR 2.00 px -> 4.70" reported vs 4.00" true). Worse, the real `fwhm` column measured by the pipeline is ignored and overwritten by the derived number, and nothing in the CSV says the value is derived.
repro: Analytics > History > click Night A - M31 > click the spreadsheet icon; open the CSV. HFR column x 2.35 == FWHM column exactly.
evidence: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv rows s1_000..s1_009; DB: select hfr,fwhm from captured_images where session_id=1 -> fwhm all NULL
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_export_service.dart:69-70 and :171; same factor in session_report_service.dart:301 (meanFwhm), capture_preview_loader.dart:180 (live capture FWHM readout), session_report.dart:36

title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is stored outside the profile data dir, so one instance offers to resume another instance's sequence
what_happened: On startup this audit instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR = /tmp/ns-audit/r-analytics/data, with ZERO rows in sequences and sequence_checkpoints) showed 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed - Sequence: New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'. The checkpoint it read is /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint, written by a DIFFERENT concurrently-running instance.
expected: Crash recovery must be scoped to the instance/profile that wrote it. Offering to resume a sequence whose id does not exist in this database is a data-integrity hazard: on a machine that runs both the desktop app and the headless host (a shipped configuration) the two silently clobber each other's recovery state, and Resume would restart the wrong run. Note also the self-contradictory summary line 'Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'.
repro: Run two Skotiq desktop instances with different SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR values. Build a sequence in one. Restart the other: it offers to recover the first one's sequence.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-33-sci2.png; sqlite3 <profile db> 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> 0 rows, 'select * from sequences' -> 0 rows; the checkpoint file in ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop was last written at 14:50 by another pid
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:347 getApplicationSupportDirectory() is passed to sequencerSetCheckpointDir, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR; native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs:516

title: BLS card gives no significance verdict, and its only significance number (SDE) scores pure noise higher than a textbook-strong periodic signal
what_happened: Three controlled runs on the same 80-point, 118.5-minute light curve in Analytics > Science > Period Analysis. (A) pure noise: Lomb-Scargle 21.2 min, power 0.07, FAP 0.3366, no badge; BLS 21.8 min, Depth -53.6 mmag, SDE 2.7. (B) injected sinusoid P=20.0 min, amplitude 0.10 mag: LS 19.8 min, power 0.97, FAP < 1e-10, badge 'Strong'; BLS 20.1 min, Depth -115.9 mmag, SDE 2.5. (C) injected box transit P=20.0 min, depth +0.150 mag, duration 2.4 min: LS 19.8 min, FAP 9.6e-5, 'Strong'; BLS 20.0 min, Depth 151.2 mmag, SDE 4.82. So the SDE of PURE NOISE (2.7) is HIGHER than the SDE of a signal the app itself calls Strong with FAP < 1e-10 (2.5), and a genuine transit only reaches 4.8. The BLS half of the card shows no badge, no threshold and no verdict of any kind - just the bare number.

title: Photometry CSV export writes local wall-clock timestamps with no timezone, silently shifting every measurement by the observer's UTC offset
what_happened: Science Data Export > Photometry Measurements > CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-18-30.csv. The first data row's Timestamp column reads '2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'. The DB row it came from has timestamp = 1785574800, which is 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z. The CSV is emitting local time (UTC-4 here) in ISO-8601 shape with no offset and no 'Z'.
expected: Photometry timestamps are the input to period analysis, AAVSO/AID submissions and any cross-observer comparison; they must be UTC (ideally JD or HJD as well) and must carry the offset. Any script that parses this file as ISO-8601 will place every point 4 hours off, and the error changes with the observer's timezone and with DST inside a single observing season.
repro: Analytics > Science > export/database icon > Photometry Measurements > CSV. Compare the Timestamp column with `select timestamp from photometry_measurements order by timestamp limit 1` (unix seconds).
evidence: CSV row: '5,148,target_primary,target,512.0,512.0,100000.0,-0.00612,120.0,0.008,false,2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'; sqlite: id 581 timestamp 1785574800 = 2026-08-01 09:00:00 UTC. The same file's own name is stamped '2026-08-02T11-18-30' (local) while the science report's footer uses Z - three conventions across the export surface.
where: the science CSV export writer used by ScienceExportHub (it calls toIso8601String() on a local DateTime rather than .toUtc())
